acceptedAnswer.text: A gyroplane (also called an autogyro) is a type of rotorcraft that uses an unpowered, freely spinning rotor for lift and an engine-driven propeller for thrust. Unlike a helicopter, the rotor is not powered during flight — it spins due to the airflow through it, a process called autorotation. Gyroplanes are known for their excellent slow-speed stability and short takeoff and landing capabilities.

Gyroplanes are considered one of the safest aircraft categories. Because the rotor autorotates continuously, a gyroplane can never stall or spin the way a fixed-wing airplane can. In the event of an engine failure, the gyroplane descends steeply but under full control and can land in a very short distance — even in a small field. Proper training with a qualified instructor like FAA-certified CFI Matt Snell at Rebel Red's Gyros is essential to fly safely.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a license to fly a gyroplane?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. In the United States, you need at minimum an FAA Sport Pilot Certificate with a gyroplane category rating, or an FAA Private Pilot Certificate with a gyroplane rating. The FAA regulates gyroplanes as light sport aircraft or as standard category aircraft depending on the model. Rebel Red's Gyros offers both Sport Pilot and Private Pilot gyroplane training with CFI Matt Snell in Lamesa, TX.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take to learn to fly a gyroplane?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most students can solo a gyroplane in 10–15 hours of flight training. Earning an FAA Sport Pilot Certificate typically requires a minimum of 20 flight hours, while a Private Pilot Certificate requires at least 40 hours. The total time to certification depends on the student's aptitude, weather, and how frequently they train.
